Examples: A video file has a player type of 'Flash'. A media object has a player type of 'Silverlight'. An audio stream has a player type of 'HTML5 Audio'.

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". Examples: "Actor's performance role characterName 'Hamlet'", "Actress's performance role characterName 'Juliet'". Distinct from character, which refers to the fictional person itself, whereas characterName is the name of the character in a specific performance.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: embeddedTextCaption
candidates.comment: An embedded text caption relation between an audio, image, or video object and the textual captioning it contains. Also called "media caption", "text overlay", "meme text". Examples: "Image object embeddedTextCaption 'Distracted Boyfriend Meme'", "Video object embeddedTextCaption 'Subtitles for foreign language'", "Audio object embeddedTextCaption 'Lyrics displayed'".

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: originalMediaContextDescription
candidates.comment: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaContextDescription 'Video was originally posted on TikTok in 2020.'", "Image Review B originalMediaContextDescription 'Photo taken during a protest in 2018, not current event.'", "Audio Review C originalMediaContextDescription 'Clip is from a satirical podcast, not a news broadcast.'". Distinct from reviewBody, which is the main text of the review.

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mediaItemAppearance
candidates.comment: A media item appearance relation between a media review item and the specific media object(s) grouped within it. Also called: associated media, media objects, grouped items. Examples: "Fact Check Item mediaItemAppearance 'Image of politician'", "Video Analysis Item mediaItemAppearance 'Clip from broadcast'", "Audio Review Item mediaItemAppearance 'Sound recording'".

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: contentSize
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a media object, indicating its file size. Also called "file size", "media size", "data size". Examples: "Image file contentSize '2.5MB'", "Video file contentSize '500MB'".

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: representativeOfPage
candidates.comment: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.

candidates.label: homeTeam
candidates.comment: A home team relation between a sports event and the team or person designated as the home participant. Also called host team, home side, local team. Examples: "A sports event has a home team 'Lions'.", "The match features a home team.", "This event's home team is a specific person."

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."
